title: {{NAME}} and the Robot Who Couldn't Sleep
moral: Everyone is a little bit scared sometimes — and a kind friend makes all the difference.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a thoughtful young boy with straight dark hair and big dark eyes, wearing a navy blue t-shirt with a circuit-board pattern, grey sweatpants, and white sneakers — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had been collecting parts for months — springs from old pens, gears from broken clocks, copper wire from the drawer in the laundry that nobody ever opened.

One Saturday afternoon, he clicked the last piece into place and stood back.

The little robot on his desk whirred. Its chest light blinked blue. Its head turned left, then right. Then it looked straight at {{NAME}} and made a sound exactly like: "Oh."

pages.content:
{{NAME}} named him Bolt.

Bolt spent the day following {{NAME}} around the room, bumping gently into chair legs, beeping at the cat, and studying the bookshelf with great seriousness.

But when night came, something went wrong.

{{NAME}} switched off his bedroom light — and Bolt's chest light went frantic. Beep beep BEEP. His little arms waved. His wheels spun in tight anxious circles.

"Oh!" said {{NAME}}. "You're scared of the dark."

pages.content:
{{NAME}} sat on the floor beside Bolt and thought carefully.

"I was scared of the dark once too," he said. "My dad put a little light in the corner and it helped."

Bolt tilted his head. Beep.

"Okay," said {{NAME}}. "Let's build you one."

They worked by the light of {{NAME}}'s torch, sorting through his parts box together. Bolt handed pieces over with his tiny claw arms. {{NAME}} soldered and fitted and tested until — a soft golden glow filled the corner of the room.

pages.content:
Bolt rolled over to the nightlight and stood very still.

His chest light slowed. Blue. Blue. Blue. One blink every few seconds — calm and steady.

He turned back to {{NAME}} and made a new sound. Not a beep this time. Something lower and longer, like a small, satisfied hum.

"Good," said {{NAME}} quietly. "Now we can both sleep."

pages.content:
{{NAME}} climbed into bed. In the corner, Bolt sat perfectly still beside his little light, humming so quietly it was almost like breathing.

The room was cosy and gold and safe.

{{NAME}} looked at Bolt for a long moment. He had built Bolt to be smart and fast and useful. He hadn't planned on building him a friend.

But that turned out to be the best part.

He closed his eyes, and Bolt hummed him all the way to sleep.
